text:
maria: Heads-up — around 03:15 UTC we saw short bursts in us-east-1 where admission allowed ~50 concurrent requests per shard, GPUs hit ~96% memory and a few pods OOMed, causing reactive spillback and longer queueing. Thinking of adding a 'short‑hold' admission lane that enforces a small per-node in‑flight cap during burst windows. Thoughts?

aj: Can you drop the quick metrics/snippets? queue depth, GPU mem, prewarm evictions?

maria: quick paste from the spike window:
```
queue_depth: 128 -> 18 (20s)
gpu_mem_util: 88% -> 96%
prewarm_evictions: 6 in 60s
avg_latency: 42ms -> 95ms (p50), p99 spiked to 1.1s
spillback_count: 42
```

aj: Looks like KV cache thrash + a burst of cold starts. Two immediate levers: reduce warm‑pool drain threshold (e.g., 70%->60%) and add a short‑hold admission slot (5s) to rate‑limit probes during the burst window. Also per‑shard spillback lanes so we don't push all load to other AZs.

daniel: We ran a small canary with short‑hold=5s on canary cluster last week — p50 +10ms, p99 unchanged and incidents cleared faster. Need a replay with synthetic bursts though.

kevin: Quick cost note: lowering drain threshold will increase idle hours. Do we have an estimate? Even +2–4% might matter for sustained weeks.

maria: rough calc: for the cluster slice impacted it's ~+3% GPU hours under steady state — but it prevents ~1–2 hour degradation incidents which are ~20–30x cost in support and SLO pain. I can model more precisely if you want.

aj: For rollout plan: 1) small canary (5% traffic) with short‑hold=5s + drain_threshold=60, 2) extra metrics: spillback_count, short_hold_blocked, warmpool_idle_hours, 3) 30m canary watch, rollback if p99 > target or warmpool idle jumps >8%.

autoscale-bot: Canary deployed to cluster-eus1-canary: short_hold=5s, drain_threshold=60% — monitoring enabled.

aj: :thumbsup: Add a Grafana panel for short_hold_blocked and alert if spillback_count > 30 in 5m. Also update runbook to call @oncall before full rollout.

maria: I'll open a PR for the runbook + alert changes, and post a canary status update in #incidents after 30m. Action items: PR (#), grafana panel, replay test, cost model.

kevin: If canary looks good, consider a staged region roll with extra buffer in older regions (apac) since network egress has higher tail latency there.

maria: noted. Thanks all — monitoring now.
